items.title: Lawrence Duhé Interview, 1957-06-09
items.q: He's a clarinet player downtown. ... Well, I went to his place too the other day.

ctx.x: Now that chorus to high society, you know, that they all played, do you know who started that? Was that a piccolo part or something?
Piku Composer. You think Piku Composer? Yeah. He's a clarinet player downtown.

items.title: Lawrence Duhé Interview, 1957-06-09
items.q: They had a colored man, Manuel Perez, all that was up there for them.

ctx.x: Yeah, the contract here says the New Orleans Jazz Band.

That must have been number two, but they had two orchestras left, but the Dixalan, you remember, bro, used to put that livery stable blue? Yeah, the rocker. Yeah, the rocker and shield. Yeah. Yeah, the ritual. They're still written in there. They had a colored man, Manuel Perez, all that was up there for them. These men, is it Mitchell Lacalze, C-A-L-Z-I?

That's the booker. He was the booker, and this Lee Krauss. Krauss, that's two partners. Two partners. They're the ones that booked you. That's correct. Into the deluxe. That's right. Yeah, that's so nice. We saw Louis Capard, have you seen him lately?
